name: AssemblyAI
description: AssemblyAI's pricing page covers speech-to-text, text-to-speech and an LLM Gateway, with a free tier and pay-as-you-go per-hour rates.
features: EU region at the same price as the US
strengths: $50 in free credits at signup, no credit card required
EU region costs the same as the US region
limitations: Free-tier streaming concurrency is limited to 5 new streams per minute

plans.name: Free tier
highlights: Up to 185 hours pre-recorded and 333 hours streaming transcription

plans.name: Pay-as-you-go
plans.note: Billed monthly on actual usage, in USD; no minimum commitment. Starting limit 100 new streams per minute.

free.details: No credit card needed to start. The pricing page says the free tier includes up to 185 hours of pre-recorded transcription and up to 333 hours of streaming transcription; 5 new streaming connections per minute.

api.summary: Pre-recorded speech-to-text per hour: Universal-3.5 Pro $0.21, Universal-2 $0.15. Text-to-Speech $15 per 1M input characters. Streaming per-hour prices are on the Realtime tab, which was not re-read.

pricing.regional: The EU region costs the same as the US region (endpoints api.eu.assemblyai.com and streaming.eu.assemblyai.com). Tax treatment: not stated.

verification.notes: Product active (speech-to-text, understanding and text-to-speech APIs). Pricing page lists pay-as-you-go per-hour rates and a custom tier. Corrected: the free tier is now described as up to 185 hours of pre-recorded and 333 hours of streaming transcription (the old '$50 credit' wording was not on the page). Streaming per-hour prices sit on a separate tab that was not re-read.
verification.method: Opened in the Claude desktop built-in browser; page text read

profile.headline: Voice AI infrastructure for developers who transcribe, understand and act on speech

capabilities.title: Transcribe recorded audio and video
capabilities.text: The pre-recorded Speech-to-Text API handles files.

capabilities.title: Transcribe live audio
capabilities.text: The real-time API covers voice agents, captions and agent assist.

capabilities.title: Build speech-to-speech agents
capabilities.text: The Voice Agent API works over a single WebSocket.

capabilities.title: Pull structured insight from transcripts
capabilities.text: The Speech Understanding API extracts structured information from what was said.

featureCards.name: Pre-recorded Speech-to-Text API
featureCards.text: Accurate transcripts of audio and video files.

featureCards.name: Guardrails
featureCards.text: PII redaction, profanity filtering and content moderation.

featureCards.name: LLM Gateway
featureCards.text: Applies frontier language models to voice workflows.

audienceDetail.text: The site is written for developers who add speech to their own applications.
Accurate speech recognition and scalable infrastructure are the stated focus.
Guardrails cover redaction of personal information and content moderation.

scenarios.title: Live captions
scenarios.text: Caption a live stream or a meeting as people speak.

scenarios.title: Agent assist
scenarios.text: Give support agents live help while they are on a call.

scenarios.title: Voice agents
scenarios.text: Build a spoken assistant on the real-time or Voice Agent API.

scenarios.title: Redact personal details
scenarios.text: Remove PII from transcripts before they are stored or shared.

gettingStarted.text: The site points new visitors to the overview of its APIs.
Choose pre-recorded or streaming speech-to-text for your case.

gettingStarted.step: Look at the Voice Agent API
gettingStarted.text: Use it if you want speech-to-speech agents.

gettingStarted.step: Check pricing and the developer docs
gettingStarted.text: Both are linked from the site.
